item.title: Demystifying evals for AI agents
item.description: Guidance on how to design more rigorous and useful evals for agents across a range of agent architectures and use cases in real-world deployment.

item.title: Designing AI-resistant technical evaluations
item.description: What we learned from three iterations of a performance engineering take-home that Claude keeps beating.

item.title: Building a C compiler with a team of parallel Claudes
item.description: Nicholas Carlini, a researcher on our Safeguards team, explains how he tasked 16 agents with writing a Rust-based C compiler, from scratch, capable of compiling the Linux kernel.

item.title: Quantifying infrastructure noise in agentic coding evals
item.description: Agentic coding benchmarks are often treated as precise measurements of relative model capability. However, we’ve found that infrastructure configuration alone can produce meaningful differences in the scores.

item.title: Eval awareness in Claude Opus 4.6’s BrowseComp performance
item.description: Evaluating Opus 4.6 on BrowseComp, we found cases where the model recognized the test, then found and decrypted answers to it—raising questions about eval integrity in web-enabled environments.

item.title: Harness design for long-running application development
item.description: Harness design is key to performance at the frontier of agentic coding. Here's how we pushed Claude further in frontend design and long-running autonomous software engineering.

item.title: How we built Claude Code auto mode: a safer way to skip permissions
item.description: Claude Code users approve 93% of permission prompts. We built classifiers to automate some decisions, increasing safety while reducing approval fatigue. Here's what it catches, and what it misses.

item.title: Scaling Managed Agents: Decoupling the brain from the hands
item.description: Harnesses encode assumptions that go stale as models improve. Managed Agents—our hosted service for long-horizon agent work—is built around interfaces that stay stable as harnesses change.

item.title: An update on recent Claude Code quality reports
item.description: We traced recent reports of Claude Code quality issues to three separate changes. Here's what happened and what we're changing.

item.title: How we contain Claude across products
item.description: As agents grow more capable, so does their potential blast radius. The engineering question is how to cap it. Here’s what we’ve learned building containment for claude.ai, Claude Code, and Cowork.

item.title: Redesigning source control at Anthropic
item.description: As our merges per day grew more than tenfold, source control became our biggest development bottleneck. Here, we share how we migrated to an in-house version control system in five months.

item.title: Introducing Claude Mythos and Fable 5.1

item.title: Strengthening our defenses against distillation attacks
item.description: Illicit distillation allows model developers to copy frontier AI capabilities without creating proportionally robust safeguards. Here, we describe how we’ve reduced the rate of distillation by more than 90%.
